correctness.rationale: Every claimed instance is finite, with 81, 149 or 274 positions. There are 2,135, 7,125 and 23,914 distinct factors, respectively. The literal-position incidence verifier visits all 85,320, 540,274, and 3,391,024 candidate triples and asserts full solution set equals each four-box union; the independent factor-coverage branch verifier finds the same sets. All letters appear, forcing at least three distinct selected positions; the exhibited triples achieve three. Finite enumeration is exhaustive for specified orders, not a proof for other orders.

value.rationale: The motivated open fine-grained invariant is the complete family of minimum factor-hitting positions, not just its minimum cardinality (already known). The explicit four disjoint Cartesian boxes classify all minimizers at three consecutive canonical ternary substitution stages (lengths 81/149/274) and provide rigorous finite benchmarks for the widely studied attractor multiplicity problem. The structure contains much more information than an isolated computed count and requires no unjustified all-order extrapolation.
